plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. It is a staple of fall gardens and is prized for tolerating light frosts.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn to early winter in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide in temperate regions; native to East Asia (China and Japan)
plants.funFact: In Japan, the chrysanthemum is the emblem of the Imperial family, and the Chrysanthemum Throne is named after it. Its festival, Kiku no Sekku, is celebrated in autumn.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, semi-deciduous tree that produces spectacular clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. Blooms often appear before the foliage fully emerges, creating a purple canopy and carpeting the ground beneath.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas earn it the nickname 'Jacaranda City', and University of Sydney students traditionally say that a jacaranda flower falling on your head means you will pass your exams.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark leaves and delicate, often fragrant flowers that open in autumn, earlier than the more common Camellia japonica. It is popular for hedges, espaliers, and woodland gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to January)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and mild climates worldwide
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and its seeds are pressed to produce camellia oil used in cooking and cosmetics.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up bare stems topped with umbels of shimmering, wavy-petaled pink flowers just as most other garden plants are fading. The strap-like leaves appear after flowering.
plants.location: Native to the Drakensberg mountains of South Africa; grown in gardens in the UK, Europe, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: The petals have a glittering, sparkly texture caused by specialized surface cells, which led to the nickname 'diamond lily' for some Nerine species.
